issues.description: Write path throws UnsupportedOperationException only after the writer is constructed and after format params are accepted, complecting 'this format is read-only' with 'this format still accepts write parameters'
issues.detail: The classes still accept full writer constructor parameters (confidenceInterval, bits, compress, mergeExec) and only fail at fieldsWriter() call time. A simpler decomposition: a read-only format type that has no writer params at all, and a separate RW subclass (which the test code already introduces). The values 'this is a reader format' and 'this is a writer format' are complected in one class.

issues.description: Dropping @Deprecated on the public class while moving it to backward_codecs loses the deprecation signal for any downstream still referencing the old FQN via SPI
issues.detail: The old class was @Deprecated in core; the moved class drops the annotation. Users migrating will silently bind via ServiceLoader to a class that now throws at write time. The 'this is legacy' fact should remain explicit data on the type, not implicit in the package name.

issues.description: Protected fields demoted to package-private weakens the abstraction boundary for the OffHeap value hierarchy
issues.detail: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues fields went from protected to package-private. The Dense/Sparse subclasses live in the same package today, so it compiles, but the type now communicates 'no extension expected' while still being abstract and public. Either make it final/sealed, or keep fields protected. Right now identity (extensible base) and access (package-only) are complected.

issues.description: Two parallel RW test subclasses (RWScalarQuantized and RWV0Hnsw) suggest the legacy format actually has versioned write behavior that isn't captured as data
issues.detail: The rename to 'Lucene99RWV0...' plus a new RW format hints at multiple historical write variants. That's a value (format version + write rules) being encoded in class names and package layout rather than as explicit data. Worth pulling versions into a small data structure so tests select a version instead of selecting a class.

issues.description: CHANGES.txt entry merges two GitHub issues onto one line, complecting 'when feature added' with 'when format deprecated'
issues.detail: GITHUB#15169 added the new codecs; GITHUB#15223 deprecates the old ones. These are two distinct facts about two distinct points in time, joined under one 'New Features' bullet. Separate entries (one Improvements/Other for the move) keep the changelog as a clean append-only log of facts.

review.summary: The move is mostly mechanical and correct, but it complects two concerns in one type: 'a format that can only read' and 'a format whose constructor still accepts writer parameters'. The cleaner decomposition is what the test code already hints at — a read-only base with no writer params, and an RW subclass for tests. Dropping @Deprecated relies on package name to carry the 'legacy' fact, which is incidental rather than explicit data on the type. The protected to package-private demotion on OffHeap values weakens an abstraction without committing to sealing it. None of these block the move; they are decomposition hygiene for a codebase that is otherwise careful about format versioning.
